result: No new art-integration blocker or recurring resource leak established. One additional Web fullscreen state behavior is proposed for backlog.

new_findings.detail: Fullscreen commands rely on a private toggled flag without observing browser fullscreen changes. After an independent browser exit, the next Alt+Enter takes the exit branch again instead of entering fullscreen.
new_findings.evidence_limit: Existing local Web build only. Not established as a freshly built merged executable. Null exit/error properties are not engine-health witnesses. Only the fullscreen state sequence is claimed.
new_findings.suggested_backlog_text: Synchronize Web fullscreen state with the browser. platform/platform_web.c:152-163 flips a private flag without observing fullscreenchange or request outcomes. A headless Chromium probe of the retained local Web build observed windowed -> Alt+Enter fullscreen -> document.exitFullscreen windowed -> next Alt+Enter still windowed -> following Alt+Enter fullscreen. The merged source retains this logic, but the retained executable's exact source revision was not established. Add a freshly built browser regression for ordinary toggles, browser-side exit and refused/deferred requests, then derive state from the browser or its fullscreen callback. This did not block the approved art delivery.
